chunks: Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, "A man owes me a right, but he denies it to me, then he entrusts me with some wealth. May I take my due from what is with him?"

key_terms.حَقٌّ: a due right or claim owed to a person
key_terms.فَيَجْحَدُنِيهِ: then he denies that right owed to me
key_terms.يَسْتَوْدِعُنِي: he entrusts me with property for safekeeping

ai.seo_question: Can someone recover a denied debt by taking from property entrusted to him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal and ethical ruling that a person may not take back his own denied right from property that has been entrusted to him as a deposit. The Imam عليه السلام defines such an act as betrayal, showing that trust must be preserved even when one has been wronged.
